clue.text: For example clean up pub with tray found in bar on the counter

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: found in says the tray sits inside the turned bar
a counter in a pub suggests the bar, but here it means counter to the usual direction, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as the word itself
a salver is a serving tray

explanation.surface: A barman spots a tray left behind the counter of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' looks like where the bar is, but it means counter to the usual direction, the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean up is a verb plus particle with its own meaning, the textbook example of this grammatical category.

clue.text: Clairvoyant on the radio joined by psychic wanting tip one will readily exploit

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard rather than read, so take a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a prophet foresees the future, like a clairvoyant

indicators.note: wanting tip means lacking its first letter, its tip

parts.note: a seer is a psychic who sees the future

explanation.surface: A radio psychic joins another clairvoyant, both keen to cash in on listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: PROPHET heard aloud is PROFIT; SEER losing its tip leaves EER.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiteer is someone who makes excessive gains by taking unfair advantage of a situation such as a shortage.

clue.text: Rumoured grass broken by Russian leader losing cool

indicators.note: broken by says the grass is split open with the other piece set inside

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: losing says these letters are dropped from the leader's name

parts.note: Vladimir Putin, the Russian president
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A rumour spreads that someone grassed on the Russian leader, who loses his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: PUTIN loses IN to leave PUT, which breaks REED into RE-PUT-ED. 'Grass' looks like the informer verb, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means said or believed to be so on hearsay, which is exactly what rumoured conveys.

clue.text: Exclusive news story lacking source for proof — Times manage with old cartoon

indicators.note: lacking says that letter is removed from the story

parts.note: a scoop is a story one paper has before its rivals

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
as in multiplication, three times four is three by four
to do is to manage or cope

explanation.surface: A newspaper scoop goes unproven while the Times copes with an outdated cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOOP without the P that starts 'proof' gives SCOO. 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scooby-Doo is the Hanna-Barbera animated series about a talking Great Dane who solves mysteries.

clue.text: Drums, changing hands — gets sly looks

indicators.note: hands here are left and right, L and R, which swap places in the word

parts.note: reels are drums or spools that thread or cable winds on

explanation.surface: A drummer swaps sticks between hands and draws knowing glances.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and L of REELS trade places: L for left and R for right are the two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a sly, suggestive or malicious way, so leers is gives such looks.

clue.text: Mice end up confined to a particular area

indicators.note: up here means in a state of upheaval, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Mice finish up stuck in one particular area of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End up' reads as a phrase, but 'up' alone is the anagram signal working on MICE END.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic describes a disease or species native or restricted to a certain region or population.

clue.text: Outside broadcast controlling system for reviewing offside decisions — on reflection it's well done

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the combined letters are read backwards
controlling means holding, so the broadcast letters go around the other piece

parts.note: OB is the television abbreviation for an outside broadcast
VAR, the video assistant referee used in football

explanation.surface: A TV pundit, after replaying a disputed offside call, praises the referee's decision.
explanation.walkthrough: VAR is football's video assistant referee, brought in to review goals and offside calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is the exclamation of approval shouted at a fine performance, meaning much the same as well done.

clue.text: Mature whiskey discounted for party

indicators.note: discounted means taken off, so this letter is removed

parts.note: to grow up is to mature
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheap aged whiskey is offered to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature whiskey' looks like a well-aged spirit, but 'Mature' is the verb phrase GROW UP and the whiskey is just its W.
explanation.definitionFit: A group is a party in the sense of a set of people together, such as a political faction or a band of travellers.

clue.text: PIN reset fraudulently after corporation identifies street urchin

indicators.note: after says the shuffled letters follow the belly

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a gut

indicators.note: fraudulently says the letters are falsified into a different order

explanation.surface: A company's PIN is reset dishonestly, and the corporation exposes a young thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but it is a paunch, GUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttersnipe is a scruffy, badly behaved child who lives on the streets, a ragamuffin.

clue.text: Misleading advert for banking facility

indicators.note: misleading means leading astray, so the letters go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A deceptive advertisement promotes a bank's lending service.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is an arrangement letting a customer take out more than their account holds, a credit service banks provide.

clue.text: Phone agent somehow to support actor, essentially representing US military establishment

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it
essentially points to the essence, the very centre of the word

parts.note: the word whose middle letter is taken

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent rings to back up a client actor.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the middle of ACTOR; the anagram of PHONE AGENT, HEPENTAGON, goes underneath it. 'Representing' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the headquarters building of the US Department of Defense in Virginia, used to stand for the military command.

clue.text: Maybe half of Jedward track's used — but initially one with separate drums

parts.note: Jedward are the Irish pop duo of identical twins John and Edward Grimes, so either is a twin

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Half of a pop duo has a track used, but with a separate drum part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drums' looks like music after 'track', but the drums here belong to a washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub is a washing machine with one drum for washing and a second for spin-drying.

clue.text: Celebrity sounds like total joke

indicators.note: sounds like says the pieces are heard, not spelt

parts.note: a sum is a total and a one is a joke, as in 'have you heard the one about...'

explanation.surface: A famous person comes across as a complete joke.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM ONE heard aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone, as in 'he's really someone now', means a person of importance or fame.

clue.text: Polish nurse embraced by English doctor

indicators.note: embraced by says the nurse is held inside the other letters

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine
EN, an Enrolled Nurse in Britain

explanation.surface: A Polish nurse is hugged by an English doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb to polish.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct and improve a text, much as you polish a piece of writing.

clue.text: Possible to work out if, on 1st of December, occasionally lunch can be eaten outside

indicators.note: 1st of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

indicators.note: outside says the edible word goes round the letters from lunch

parts.note: edible means fit to be eaten

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: the word whose alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A picnic plan: whether lunch can occasionally be eaten outdoors in December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes the second and fourth letters of 'lunch'. 'Eaten outside' looks like al fresco dining, but 'outside' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deducible means able to be inferred or reasoned out from the evidence available.

clue.text: Dedication of mounted police unit imprisoning drunk Nigel Farage at last

indicators.note: imprisoning says the reversed unit holds the shuffled name inside
in a down clue mounted means going up, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the name's letters reel into a new order
at last means take the final letter

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Mounted police show dedication by locking up a drunken Nigel Farage at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted police' suggests horses, but 'mounted' turns the unit upwards in this down clue, and 'drunk' scrambles the name before it is locked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence is careful, persistent effort and application to a task, which is dedication.

clue.text: Dog pound opens for hip-hop artist

indicators.note: a support act opens for the main act, so this piece comes first

parts.note: to pound is to beat
a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog pound opens up for a rapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog pound' reads as an animal shelter, but the two words split and their order is swapped by 'opens for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beatboxer imitates drum machines and percussion with the mouth, a core skill in hip-hop performance.

clue.text: A Western power disrupting constitutional vote

indicators.note: disrupting means breaking into, so these letters are put inside the walk

parts.note: a constitutional is a short walk taken for health, a stroll
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A Western power upsets a vote on a constitutional question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks like it concerns a constitution, but it is a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an unofficial vote or quick show of opinion taken to gauge feeling.

clue.text: See 20
Property covered by revolutionary graffiti artist

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
covered by says the answer lies concealed within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An asset is daubed by a rebel street artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Property covered' as the definition, but 'covered by' is the hiding signal and 'Property' alone defines; TIART sits across 'graffiti artist' and turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or characteristic, which is one meaning of property.

clue.text: In retirement, focus of civil servant is touring Italy's capital city by the Med

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters are read in reverse
touring means travelling round, so the other letters go round this one
the focus is the centre, so take the middle letter

parts.note: the word whose middle letter is taken
a valet is a manservant

indicators.note: capital means the head or top letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A retired civil servant takes a tour of Rome before settling by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: V (centre of CIVIL) plus VALET goes round I to make VIVALET, which read backwards gives the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is Israel's second-largest city, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Be left at home meeting unmarried recluse

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: un-married means with M, the abbreviation for married, taken away

parts.note: a hermit lives alone, a recluse

explanation.surface: Someone who stays at home meets a single loner.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property when someone dies, that is, to be left it in a will.

clue.text: Harry Maguire shown party

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters are pushed into a new order

explanation.surface: The England footballer Harry Maguire is pictured at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the footballer's first name, but it is the verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A house-warming is a celebration held to mark moving into a new home.

clue.text: Judge is more chilling when less secure

indicators.note: less means minus, so this piece is taken away

parts.note: wintrier means colder, more like winter
to win something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A judge grows colder when feeling insecure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less secure' reads as anxious, but it is WINTRIER minus WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is one who tries a case or examines something, a judge.

clue.text: Volkswagen sack drivers found in here?

parts.note: the Golf is a Volkswagen car model
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: A Volkswagen boot holds a sack, so maybe the motorists are inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists after the car, but here they are golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's long-hitting clubs, called drivers, are carried in this bag around the course.

clue.text: Issue taking sport to get scholarship

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the sport goes inside

parts.note: an edition is one issue of a publication
RU, rugby union

explanation.surface: A magazine issue covering sport wins an academic award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scholarship' looks like a grant, but it means learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning acquired through study, the sense of scholarship as knowledge.

clue.text: Six superheroes, say — but not minute one who flies in present-day team

definitions.text: one who flies in present-day team

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: not means without, so this letter is taken out

parts.note: the X-Men are a team of Marvel superheroes, an example

explanation.surface: Six superheroes, but no one tiny, fly in a modern team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present-day' hides the pun: the team delivers presents on Christmas Day, Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vixen is one of Santa Claus's flying reindeer, who pull his sleigh on the day gifts arrive.

clue.text: Average beer upset enthusiast

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A mediocre beer disappoints a keen drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: An eager beaver is an informal idiom for a person who is very keen and hard-working.
